purpose: Define how CYNIC keeps its MCP surface fresh asynchronously when organism capabilities, exposure declarations, or MCP source code change.
invariants: MCP is a projection surface, not the organism source of truth.
The controller must detect stale, missing, or failed MCP readiness without compiling on a cortex machine.
Refresh requests must be asynchronous Kernel mempool tasks using the registry mcp-reload profile.
Successful refresh requires dispatch read-back plus a subsequent freshness proof.
Capability exposure changes in infra/agent-exposure.json are trigger inputs for MCP refresh planning.
The controller must debounce repeat refresh requests to avoid mempool floods.

freshness_statuses.failed: dispatch mcp-reload unless failure is configuration-only

proof_requirements: mcp-reload dispatch returns a task id or duplicate pending read-back
completed task is visible through Kernel agent task read-back
organ-forge emits an observation for refresh decision and refresh result
